prompt.context_jp: 清美とその幼なじみたちは、いつもの喫茶店の一角に集まっていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 清美とその幼なじみたち___、いつもの喫茶店の一角に集まっていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle that marks Kiyomi and friends as the established topic of the opening scene.

feedback.correct_en: は presents 'Kiyomi and her friends' as the scene's established topic — the narrator is setting the stage, not introducing them as new information.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make them sound newly spotted/identified, as if answering 'who gathered?'; を doesn't fit an intransitive 集まっていた.

contrast_examples.en: Kiyomi (as topic) was at the café.
It was Kiyomi who was at the café. (new info)

prompt.context_jp: 何気ない世間話のような雰囲気のなか、葉月がふとしたきっかけで口を開いた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 何気ない世間話のような雰囲気のなか、葉月___ふとしたきっかけで口を開いた。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle that introduces Hazuki as the one who suddenly starts talking.

feedback.correct_en: が marks Hazuki as the new participant whose action breaks into the scene — 'it was Hazuki who spoke up.' The reader's attention lands on her for the first time here.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would frame Hazuki as an already-established topic, flattening the suddenness; に doesn't fit a subject role here.

prompt.context_jp: 「みずぽん 超能力者なんですよ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「みずぽん___超能力者なんですよ」
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits in the dropped-particle casual reveal about Mizupon?

feedback.correct_en: The sentence is an 'A は B だ' identification: Hazuki is telling the others what Mizupon is. は presents Mizupon as the topic the predicate 超能力者 describes.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would answer 'who is the psychic?' (exhaustive listing), but here Hazuki is characterizing Mizupon, not picking her out from candidates.

contrast_examples.jp: みずぽんは超能力者だ。
みずぽんが超能力者だ。
contrast_examples.en: Mizupon is the psychic (not the others).

prompt.context_jp: 照明の落ちた廊下を、瑞稀は息を殺して進んでいた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 心臓の音___やけに大きく響き、額にはうっすらと汗がにじんだ。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits for 'the heartbeat' at this tense moment?

feedback.correct_en: が marks a sudden sensory event breaking into awareness — the heartbeat is newly felt/noticed as unusually loud. Perceptual arrivals like this take が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would turn the heartbeat into an abstract topic ('as for heartbeats…'), losing the in-the-moment surge the scene needs.

prompt.context_jp: 葉月だけが、腕組みをしたまま納得のいかない顔をしている。
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼にはまだ、譲れないひとつのこだわり___あるようだった。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle for 'one principle' in an existence clause.

feedback.correct_en: With ある introducing something new into the discourse, が is standard — the narrator is revealing a hitherto unmentioned sticking point.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would presuppose this particular こだわり is already a topic, but it's being introduced here for the first time.

contrast_examples.en: There is a sticking point. (new info)

prompt.context_jp: 「ていうかさ 宇宙人と未来人と 超能力者がいる町ってヤバくない？」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「宇宙人と未来人と 超能力者___いる町ってヤバくない？」
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle in the relative clause 'a town where X exist.'

feedback.correct_en: Inside a relative clause ('a town where ___ exist'), the subject of いる takes が. は generally can't live inside a noun-modifying clause as the subject marker.
feedback.incorrect_en: は wouldn't normally appear here because this isn't a main-clause topic — it's a subject embedded in 町 modification.

prompt.context_jp: だが画面に触れた高橋の指先が、何度スワイプしても反応は返ってこなかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼の顔___、少しずつ血の気が引いていく。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle after 彼の顔 in this descriptive line.

feedback.correct_en: 血の気が引く is specifically 顔から blood 'draws away from' — から marks the source. The subject (血の気) already takes が later in the clause.
feedback.incorrect_en: は/が wouldn't give the directional 'from his face' reading needed for this idiom.

contrast_examples.en: The color drains from his face.

prompt.context_jp: 証明されたはずのみずぽんの力を前にしても、葉月の表情は微塵も変わらなかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 証明されたはずのみずぽんの力を前にしても、葉月の表情___微塵も変わらなかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle marking Hazuki's expression here.

feedback.correct_en: は carries contrastive force: others reacted, but his expression (unlike theirs) didn't change at all. The 〜ても…微塵も〜ない frame is a classic contrastive-は environment.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make it a neutral event report, losing the 'in contrast to the others' nuance the narration needs.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼の表情は変わらなかった。

prompt.context_jp: 「いや だって そもそもね あの子たち 俺の宇宙人を 信じてないからね」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「あの子たち 俺の宇宙人___信じてないからね」
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle for '(my) alien [status]' as the thing they don't believe.

feedback.correct_en: 信じる takes を for its direct object (what is believed). Takahashi is saying they don't believe his alien-ness.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark a subject, not an object; に is for the person/entity you place trust in (信じる is normally を-marked for the content).

prompt.context_jp: 市長 梅本雅子の自己紹介のナレーション。
prompt.prompt_jp: 私のモットー___市民に寄り添う政治。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle for 'my motto' in this defining statement.

feedback.correct_en: 'A は B' is the canonical defining pattern: 'my motto IS politics close to citizens.' は sets up the motto as topic and gives its definition.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would answer 'which thing is the motto?' (identification among choices), not fitting a self-introduction definition.

contrast_examples.en: It's reading that is the hobby. (odd here)

prompt.context_jp: 従業員たちの生活は保障された。むしろ 今より環境は よくなる 高橋さん以外は
prompt.prompt_jp: むしろ 今より環境___よくなる。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle for 'the environment (compared to now)'.

feedback.correct_en: は carries contrast against the fear implicit in the earlier worry: 'contrary to expectations, the environment (at least) gets better.' Pairs naturally with むしろ.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would simply report an event without the 'reversal of expectation' nuance that むしろ sets up.

prompt.context_jp: 「あそこって どこが 買い取るんでしたっけ？」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「あそこって どこ___買い取るんでしたっけ？」
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle after どこ in this question.

feedback.correct_en: Question words like どこ, だれ, なに take が when they ARE the thing being asked about — the answer slot. は can't attach to a question word in this role.
feedback.incorrect_en: どこは is ungrammatical for 'which (place) is the one that…'; を doesn't match the subject role of 買い取る here.

prompt.context_jp: 「いや でも 実際 村上さんが言うとおりには なってるわけだし」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「実際 村上さん___言うとおりには なってるわけだし」
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle for Murakami inside the relative clause 'as Murakami says'.

feedback.correct_en: Inside the noun-modifying clause 言うとおり ('the way X says'), the subject takes が. は can't appear as the subject marker inside this kind of embedded clause.
feedback.incorrect_en: 村上さんは would try to make him the main-clause topic, breaking the 言うとおり modification.

contrast_examples.en: It is just as he says.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼は言うとおりにした。

prompt.context_jp: あやにゃんの旦那さんが市の職員だという事実は、いま彼女たちに欠けていた最後のピースかもしれなかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: あやにゃんの旦那さん___市の職員だという事実は…
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle inside the 〜という事実 clause.

feedback.correct_en: Inside the embedded content clause 〜という事実, the subject takes が. The outer 事実 is the topic (marked by は later), so the inner subject must be が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は inside this noun-modifying content would clash with the outer 事実は topic marking.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼が犯人だという事実。
contrast_examples.en: The fact that he is the culprit.

prompt.context_jp: 「うん うちの旦那 都市計画担当だからさ レイクホテルの件も 何か 絶対 知ってると思う」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「うちの旦那___都市計画担当だからさ…」
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle for 'my husband' in Aya-nyan's casual explanation.

feedback.correct_en: She's characterizing her husband (he's in urban planning) — a classic 'A は B だ' topic+comment, giving background info. In speech it's often dropped, but if a particle appears it's は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would spotlight him as newly identified ('it's my husband who is in charge'), but she's just offering context, not picking him out.

contrast_examples.jp: うちの旦那は銀行員です。
contrast_examples.en: My husband is a banker. (describing him)

contrast_examples.jp: うちの旦那が担当です。
contrast_examples.en: My husband is the one in charge. (identification)

prompt.context_jp: 「みずぽん ああいう データとか普通に消せるんですよ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「みずぽん ああいう データとか普通に___んですよ」
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the verb form that fits Hazuki's claim about Mizupon's ability.

feedback.correct_en: 消せる is the potential form ('can erase'), which matches the context of describing an ability.
feedback.incorrect_en: 消す is just 'erases' (plain action, no ability nuance); 消える is intransitive 'disappears' — Mizupon isn't the one disappearing.

prompt.context_jp: 「はい 選んでは消せないんで 全部なんですよ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「はい ___消せないんで 全部なんですよ」
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the phrase meaning 'can't pick and choose'.

feedback.correct_en: 〜ては + negative potential conveys 'can't do X selectively' — here 'I can't erase them selectively', so it has to be all-or-nothing.
feedback.incorrect_en: 選んでも消せない would mean 'even if I choose, I can't erase' — close but shifts the meaning; 選ぶのに doesn't fit the structure.

contrast_examples.en: I can't pick and choose when buying.
Even if I choose, I can't buy it.

prompt.context_jp: 高橋はスマホをしぶしぶ差し出しながら、データだけは絶対に消さないでほしいと念を押した。
prompt.prompt_jp: 高橋はスマホを___差し出しながら、…念を押した。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the adverb that captures Takahashi's reluctant handing-over.

feedback.correct_en: しぶしぶ means 'reluctantly, unwillingly' — exactly Takahashi's mood as he hands over his phone fearing data loss.
feedback.incorrect_en: すらすら = smoothly/fluently; ぺらぺら = chatting fluently. Neither captures reluctance.

prompt.context_jp: スマホの液晶は、うんともすんとも言わなかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: スマホの液晶は、___言わなかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the idiomatic phrase meaning 'didn't respond at all'.

feedback.correct_en: うんともすんとも言わない is a set idiom: not a peep, no response whatsoever. Perfectly fits a dead phone screen.
feedback.incorrect_en: The other options aren't fixed expressions for 'no response at all.'

contrast_examples.jp: 返事はうんともすんともない。

prompt.context_jp: 長く胸のうちにひとつの秘密を患ってきた高橋にとって、この職場を失うことの重みは他人にはうかがい知れないほどのものだった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 長く胸のうちにひとつの秘密を___きた高橋にとって…
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the verb that collocates with 秘密 for 'has long carried a secret.'

feedback.correct_en: 患う ('suffer from, be afflicted by') is used figuratively here — he has long been afflicted by holding a secret inside, treating it like a chronic ailment of the heart.
feedback.incorrect_en: 預かる = keep (for someone else); 借りる = borrow. Neither captures the long-held burden of a secret.

contrast_examples.en: To be afflicted by a secret in one's heart.

prompt.context_jp: この素材さえ手に入れば大きな仕事になるという___めいた気配が、岸本の背中には張りついていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: この素材さえ手に入れば…という___めいた気配。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the noun that fits 'a sense of ___-like conviction'.

feedback.correct_en: 確信めいた = 'resembling conviction/certainty.' The scene describes Kishimoto's conviction that this material will land him a big job.
feedback.incorrect_en: 確認 = confirmation (checking something), 確率 = probability. Neither captures the inner certainty hinted at here.

prompt.context_jp: How Mizupon describes HOW she erases data.
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds more natural as Mizupon's shy explanation of her method?

choices.text: 普通に こう… 手 当てるだけなんですけど
普通に こう… 手を置くだけなんですけど

feedback.correct_en: 手を当てる is the natural collocation for 'placing a hand on something' with intent (healing, touching to activate). It matches the quasi-mystical 'laying on hands' feel.
feedback.incorrect_en: 手を置く is grammatical but neutral/physical ('put a hand down'); it loses the sense of applying/pressing a hand with purpose that 当てる conveys.

contrast_examples.en: Put a hand to the forehead.
Rest a hand on the desk.

prompt.context_jp: Hazuki refusing to let Mizupon test her powers on his phone.
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds more natural as Hazuki's casual, exasperated refusal?

choices.text: はぁ？ ダメに決まってんじゃん
はぁ？ ダメに決まっているのではないか

feedback.correct_en: ダメに決まってんじゃん uses casual contractions (きまっている→きまってん, ではないか→じゃん) that fit friends joking at a café.
feedback.incorrect_en: The B version is grammatically fine but stiff/written — out of place among childhood friends over coffee.

contrast_examples.jp: 行くに決まってんじゃん。
行くに決まっているではないか。

prompt.context_jp: 由美が議論を切り上げようとして。
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds more natural for 'isn't it a waste of time to debate this now?'

choices.text: 今 そこで議論するのって 時間が もったいなくないですか？
今 そこで議論するのって 時間を もったいなくないですか？

feedback.correct_en: もったいない is an i-adjective taking が for the thing wasted: 時間がもったいない ('time is wasteful/precious to waste'). This is the fixed pattern.
feedback.incorrect_en: 時間を もったいない is ungrammatical because もったいない isn't a verb; the 'wasted' thing takes が, not を.

prompt.context_jp: Reassuring Takahashi that Aya-nyan will take his secret seriously.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds more natural for 'she'll be more sympathetic'?

choices.text: より親身になってくれますよ
より親切な人になってくれますよ

feedback.correct_en: 親身になる is the set phrase meaning 'take (someone's situation) to heart; be genuinely sympathetic/caring.' It fits Kiyomi's point that Aya-nyan will treat the matter personally.
feedback.incorrect_en: 親切な人になる literally means 'become a kind person' — awkward here because Aya-nyan already is kind; the issue is her engagement with the specific issue.

contrast_examples.jp: 親身になって相談に乗る。

prompt.context_jp: Takahashi greeting Aya-nyan's husband after 7 years.
prompt.prompt_en: Which opening is more natural for a polite reunion after a long gap?

choices.text: ご無沙汰しております お忙しいとこ すみません
久しぶりだね お忙しいとこ すみません

feedback.correct_en: ご無沙汰しております is the standard polite 'it's been a while' used with someone you don't see often and want to show respect to — fits a first proper exchange after seven years.
feedback.incorrect_en: 久しぶりだね is casual peer-to-peer; mixing it with the polite お忙しいとこすみません creates a jarring register clash.

contrast_examples.jp: ご無沙汰しております。
